propositions: When two bundle objects exist for the same ref in S3, git-remote-s3 helper rejects push and clone operations fail with 'multiple updates for ref' or 'multiple bundles exists on server', making the remote unclonable and push unretryable, because the ref becomes ambiguous.

Upstream git-s3 doctor is interactive-only (blocking input() on EOF) and discards the non-chosen bundle head to a new orphan ref, losing any events unique to that head—unacceptable for an append-only event log.

Rebar already implements lossless multi-parent merge reconciliation for git remotes via sync._union_merge and _do_reconverge, using 2-parent merges per target ref and .gitattributes merge=ours for derived caches; this semantics must be reused for S3 bundles without discard.

An optional s3_doctor.py module must detect multi-bundle state, acquire the helper's per-ref conditional-put lock, fetch all divergent bundle heads, fold them via iterated 2-parent merges (never octopus), write the merged result as a new bundle, delete the originals only after the merge is durable, and never delete the merged tip—guaranteeing at least one lossless bundle at every crash point.

Multi-process contention is safe because exactly one doctor wins the helper's S3 lock and collapses bundles; other processes back off and converge via the subsequent push retry on the single collapsed bundle, with no reinvented lock or rebar boto3 dependency (boto3 ships transitively under the optional [s3] extra).

The heal must run under rebar's write_lock during the local merge to prevent interleaving with concurrent local committers, with the helper's S3 lock as the outer (cross-clone) serialization point and write_lock as the inner (per-tracker) lock, establishing a fixed cycle-free order.
